# cachyos-coder-tools

The **minimal CachyOS tool gate** — four of the six layer candies that the retired non-CachyOS coder
workstations were the only live proof of, on the CachyOS (`x86_64_v3`) base, and nothing else.

It lives in the **`opencharly/distro-cachyos`** repo as `box/cachyos-coder-tools`.

## Why this image exists

The org retired every non-CachyOS coder workstation (`fedora-coder`, `debian-coder`,
`ubuntu-coder`) and their three pod beds. Those three beds were the **single** live gate for six
layer candies — `layer-pixi`, `layer-language-runtimes`, `layer-typst`, `layer-github-actions`,
`layer-google-cloud-npm`, `layer-grafana-tools`. Measured, not assumed: no other bed in the org
composes any of them, and each of their own repos declares no `pod:`/`vm:` entity at all, so
dropping the coder beds without a replacement would have left six layer repos with no live proof
whatsoever (R7).

This image is that replacement. It is deliberately **minimal**: it proves four of those six candies and
does not resurrect the workstation the cutover retires.

**`layer-rpmfusion` is deliberately absent, and cannot be added.** RPM Fusion is a Fedora package
repository driven end-to-end by `dnf` / `rpmkeys` / `rpm -E %fedora`; there is no Arch or CachyOS
analogue, so it keeps its own minimal Fedora bed (`distro-fedora`'s `fedora-rpmfusion`).

## Why it is not the full coder stack

The first draft of this image composed `fedora-coder`'s entire 26-candy stack, candy-for-candy,
so the two would stay comparable. **It could not build.** The composed
`ai.opencharly.description` label reached **121,320 bytes on a single generated Containerfile
line**, over buildkit's hard **65,535-byte per-line limit**:

```
error: failed to solve: dockerfile line greater than max allowed size of 65535
```

The image's intermediate stages built fine (their description label is ~2.4 KB), so the ceiling is
a function of the candy-chain size, not of the CachyOS base. That is a genuine product limit on how
large an image's composed label may grow — `opencharly/spec#293` carries the evidence, alongside its
containerd-side sibling (the same label over 4096 bytes blocks a `engine: containerd` pod start).
This image stays far under both caps by composing exactly the candies it exists to prove.

## Box Properties

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Base | `cachyos` (the base box at `box/cachyos`, `docker.io/cachyos/cachyos-v3` pinned by digest) |
| Pkg | `pac` |
| Distro tags | `[cachyos, arch]` — inherited from the base; every candy's arch section applies |
| Builders | `pixi` / `npm` / `cargo` / `aur` → `arch.arch-builder`, inherited from the base |
| Platforms | `linux/amd64` |
| User | `user` / uid 1000 — **created, not adopted** (CachyOS ships no pre-existing uid-1000 account and declares no `base_user:`) |
| Home | `/home/user` |
| Registry | `ghcr.io/opencharly` |

## Composition

`cachyos-app-skills` (this image's skill carrier) · `pod-sshd` · `layer-pixi` ·
`layer-language-runtimes` · `layer-typst` · `layer-github-actions`

The two of the six it does NOT compose are named in "Why this image exists" and in the
bed's own comment: `google-cloud-npm` and `grafana-tools`, each blocked by a filed candy defect.

`pod-sshd` is there so the pod has a long-running service to deploy and probe. Ports are
**inherited from the candy chain** (the box declares none); host mappings are auto-allocated on
`127.0.0.1` at deploy.

## Verification

```bash
charly -C box/cachyos box validate                                # schema + composition
charly -C box/cachyos box build cachyos-coder-tools               # build on the CachyOS base
charly -C box/cachyos box inspect cachyos-coder-tools --format base    # → cachyos
charly -C box/cachyos check run check-cachyos-coder-tools-pod     # the R10 bed
```

The bed `check-cachyos-coder-tools-pod` (in this repo's `charly.yml`, `disposable: true`) is the
functional evidence: it builds the image, deploys it, runs every composed candy's baked check, and
adds one representative **binary** assertion per compensated candy —
`/usr/local/bin/pixi`, `/usr/local/bin/typst`, `/usr/bin/act`, `/usr/local/bin/actionlint`,
`/usr/bin/dotnet`, `/usr/bin/php`, `/usr/bin/python3` — seven distinct paths, plus a
base-identity probe.

That binary set is the point: a candy whose per-distro section silently no-ops on CachyOS (the
`sdk#453` failure mode, where a layer's `distro:` package section applies nothing and the image
still builds clean) cannot pass the bed. Each candy check would pass in isolation either way; only a
composition-level assert catches the no-op.
